claim: Regent's Park Open Air Theatre 2026 summer season runs 2 May to 19 September, including a world-premiere Sherlock Holmes (May–Jun), A Midsummer Night's Dream (Jun–Jul), the first UK revival of Cats (25 Jul–12 Sep) and family show Anansi the Spider.
quote: The 2026 season at Regent's Park Open Air Theatre opens on 2 May and runs through 19 September... CATS, the first ever UK revival, directed and choreographed by Drew McOnie.

claim: BST Hyde Park runs 27 June–12 July 2026 in Hyde Park with headliners Garth Brooks, ATEEZ, Maroon 5, Mumford & Sons, Duran Duran, Pitbull and two Lewis Capaldi nights.
quote: BST Hyde Park returns in 2026 with performances from artists including Garth Brooks, ATEEZ, Maroon 5, Mumford & Sons, Duran Duran, Pitbull and Lewis Capaldi running from 27 June to 12 July.

claim: Serpentine Lido in Hyde Park is a seasonal open-water swim spot typically open daily from June to mid-September with weekend sessions from mid-May.
quote: Swimming at the Serpentine Lido is a seasonal highlight, usually running from June to mid-September, with weekend sessions available from mid-May.

claim: Hampstead Heath bathing ponds use bookable sessions via Xn Leisure for summer 2026, with bookings opening 26 May for sessions starting 2 June; advance booking is essential on warm weekends.
quote: For Summer 2026, bookings will be made through Xn Leisure, opening at 12 noon on Tuesday 26 May for sessions starting on Tuesday 2 June.

claim: Richmond Park is London's largest royal park at 2,500 acres and home to a herd of around 630–650 red and fallow deer roaming freely.
quote: Richmond Park is London's largest royal park, covering 2,500 acres... home to a herd of 650 deer – and all within a short distance of central London.

claim: Visitors to Richmond Park must keep a 50m distance from deer, and dogs must be on leads from 1 May to 31 July during birthing season; fawns are typically born May–June.
quote: dogs must be kept on leads in Richmond and Bushy parks during deer birthing season, which runs from 1 May – 31 July each year... all visitors must observe a minimum 50m distance.

claim: Uber Boat by Thames Clippers operates the RB1 and RB6 routes serving 24 piers from Putney/Battersea to Barking Riverside, passing Westminster, the London Eye, Tower Bridge and Greenwich — doubling as commuter transport and sightseeing.
quote: Uber Boat by Thames Clippers stops at 24 piers along the Thames between Barking Riverside Pier in the East and Putney Pier in the West.

claim: Hop-on Hop-off all-day Thames Clippers passes are the best-value sightseeing option, with kids going free on family tickets when accompanying two adults.
quote: With a Family Hop-on Hop-off ticket kids go free, with two adults and up to three children (5 to 15 years old) able to hop on and hop off all day.

claim: The Greenwich Foot Tunnel is a free 366m pedestrian tunnel open 24 hours linking Island Gardens on the Isle of Dogs to Cutty Sark on the south bank, with lifts and stairs at each entrance.
quote: Greenwich Foot Tunnel is open 24 hours a day. There are stairs and lifts at each entrance.

claim: The Royal Observatory, National Maritime Museum, Queen's House and Cutty Sark sit within walking distance in Greenwich; the Foot Tunnel exits at Island Gardens for the classic 'Canaletto view' of the Old Royal Naval College and Observatory.
quote: the famous 'Canaletto view' of Greenwich, where you can see the sensational Old Royal Naval College on the river front, framing the iconic Queen's House and the Royal Observatory behind them on top of the hill.

claim: Kew Gardens is a UNESCO World Heritage Site of 326 acres with 50,000+ living plants; peak-season adult tickets are around £20 weekday/£22 weekend (online) and summer weekends close as late as 8 pm.
quote: Peak Season (1 February to 31 October) pricing: £20 (Online weekday); £22 (Weekend and bank holidays, online price).

claim: The 2026 Serpentine Pavilion, 'A Serpentine' by Mexico City studio LANZA Atelier, opens 6 June 2026 at Serpentine South and remains until October — a free outdoor attraction in Kensington Gardens.
quote: The pavilion will open to the public on 6 June 2026 at Serpentine South. The pavilion will remain on view through October 2026.

claim: The Diana, Princess of Wales Memorial Playground in Kensington Gardens reopens for summer 2026 after a £3 million Royal Parks renewal.
quote: The Diana, Princess of Wales Memorial Playground will be closed for a major renewal and will reopen for Summer 2026. The Royal Parks charity is undertaking a £3 million renewal.

claim: ZSL London Zoo on the northern edge of Regent's Park is open daily through summer (10am–6pm) and runs adults-only Zoo Nights with street food, talks and cocktails; 2026 also marks ZSL's 200th anniversary.
quote: During summer (March 28 - September 2, 2026), the zoo is open from 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM... Zoo Nights (adults only).

claim: The South Bank stretch of the Thames Path from Westminster to Tower Bridge is the most sightseer-friendly walking section, passing the London Eye, National Theatre, Tate Modern, Millennium Bridge and Shakespeare's Globe.
quote: Westminster Bridge to Tower Bridge is the sightseer's walk through Central London... you'll encounter modern structures, including Tate Modern, the Millennium Footbridge and the London Eye.

claim: Taste of London food festival returns to The Regent's Park 17–21 June 2026 with leading restaurants, bars and chef demos in an open-air setting.
quote: Taste of London returns to The Regent's Park from 17-21 June, featuring superstar chefs, the hottest restaurants in town, and next level bars.
